answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: let the challenge probing adapt: it keeps issuing tasks the fleet already failed, because ember only stays cheap while repeat infrastructure gets no useful signal and its pass rate degrades each epoch. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
